messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: region=nyc3 full outage detected — control plane and worker nodes reporting 100% loss, scheduler errors spiking. (alert_id=INC-1742008453)

alex: seeing the same on dashboards. All nyc3 node pools show `NotReady`. LB healthchecks failing, 502s from edge. Anyone on-call for networking?

priya: I'm on it. Starting with provider console and BGP status. Can someone run quick health checks for k8s API reachability?

mike: running from my laptop:
```
$ kubectl --context=nyc3 get nodes
Error from server: the server is currently unable to handle the request (get nodes)
```
No API access.

jess: checking datadog metrics — control-plane latency jumped then dropped to 0. No control-plane heartbeats after 1742008400.

sam: provider status page shows an ongoing network fabric incident in nyc3: "intermittent packet loss between racks -> escalated". Opening support case now, attaching logs.

network-bot: BGP peers: 3/6 down for nyc3-edge. Flows show blackholing on two peering routers. (see: https://provider.status/incident/6789)

priya: thanks. escalation to provider support with severity P1. Requesting immediate traffic shift — we should start moving live traffic to eu-west1 and us-west2.

alex: agree. Initiate weighted failover via global LB. Proposed plan: shift 80% to eu-west1, 20% to us-west2 for redundancy, then drain nyc3. Any objections?

mike: no objections. Reminder: some customers are pinned to nyc3 via routing policy — we need to identify and migrate them or temporarily override. I'll pull list now.

jess: note: prefix cache keys for many requests are in Redis in nyc3. Shifting traffic will increase latency for cached prefixes until cross-region cache warmup completes.

sam: I've started support chat. Provider suggests BGP flap mitigation but not ETA. They recommended traffic reroute.

ops-oncall: executing reroute. Commands:
```
$ lbctl update --global --weights eu-west1=80 us-west2=20
$ lbctl flush-healthchecks --region nyc3
```
I'll push now, will monitor for error spikes.

alex: while ops reroutes, let's prepare failover for model-serving. We should enable fallback model variant (quantized L2) in eu-west1 to handle extra load.

mike: patching rollout: set default model pool to eu-west1-quantized, canary 5% first. Patch:
```
PATCH /v1/route/serve
{ "default_pool": "eu-west1-quantized", "canary": 5 }
```

priya: provider support responding: they see control-plane isolation between two core routers; manual intervention ongoing. No ETA yet. They've requested we keep traffic off nyc3.

jess: alerting SRE pager and sending short notice to support@ and CSMs. Draft: "We are failing over traffic from nyc3 due to provider network outage. Expect degraded latencies for EU/US cross-region requests. Will update in 15m." Anyone edit?

sam: add note about embeddings jobs — long-running batch jobs scheduled in nyc3 should be paused to avoid resource contention and retries.

ops-oncall: reroute applied. Immediate drop in 502s from 70%->15%. Latency to eu-west1 increased tail by ~120ms but overall errors down.

alex: good. Next steps: 1) finish draining nyc3 nodes (don't terminate; cordon+drain) 2) pause scheduled batch jobs 3) verify canaries for model fallback 4) keep provider engagement until full restore.

mike: running node drain:
```
kubectl --context=nyc3 cordon node-nyc3-1
kubectl --context=nyc3 drain node-nyc3-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Started for first node.

priya: provider update: hardware level fix being applied to routers now, they expect partial restoration in ~30-45m. They will notify when BGP sessions fully return.

jess: observing a few customers reporting auth-token failures — likely due to session affinity tied to nyc3. Workaround: clear affinity cookies via edge config for affected routes.

alex: ops, can you spin short-lived extra capacity in eu-west1 (2x worker pools) to accelerate draining and absorb extra load? We'll reconcile cost later.

ops-oncall: provisioning additional pools now. ETA ~6min to be up. Note: this will incur burst instance charges on the account.

sam: CSMs updated. I'll compile list of customers pinned to nyc3 and coordinate temporary routing override where needed.

mike: can we enable auto-fallback to CPU for low-priority replicas if GPU pools in eu-west1 saturate? We should avoid request failures even if slower.

alex: yes — enable CPU fallback for non-ML-critical routes. Patch will set priority:
1) GPU eu-west1-quantized
2) GPU us-west2
3) CPU eu-west1

ops-oncall: CPU fallback enabled.

network-bot: BGP peers recovering: 5/6 established. Flow checks improving.

priya: provider confirms BGP full convergence in progress. They will monitor for 15m then lift fabric isolation ticket.

jess: rolling post-incident banner to status.redwood.ai with initial update and ETA from provider.

sam: collecting postmortem notes as we go. Key items to record: detection triggers, routing policy gaps for pinned customers, cross-region cache warmup strategy, cost impact from burst capacity.

alex: great work. Keep updates in thread. If provider restores and stability holds for 30m, we'll mark incident mitigated and start planned recovery steps (reverse weights slowly, warm caches, resume batch jobs). If not, escalate to exec on-call.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1742008453 acknowledged by alex, priya, ops-oncall. Channel: #incidents. Thread will be auto-archived after resolution.
